subject: [PATCH v2 4/4] sched/numa: do not let VMA PID activity gate promotion

2026-09-11.patch_summary: This patch prevents VMA PID activity from gating memory promotion in NUMA-aware scheduling. It introduces a new field to track the sequence ID of socket-placement scans and allows periodic placement scans to avoid starvation. The change is motivated by a scenario where a large shmem VMA occupied each scan, causing 84 GB of VMAs to be skipped as inactive. The patch fixes a previous commit that enhanced vma scanning logic and improves memory tiering in multi-threaded applications.

reviews.author: Peter Zijlstra
reviews.summary: Reviewer Peter Zijlstra expressed strong disagreement with the tiering code, stating he's 'not a fan' of its effects, but acknowledged that it might be acceptable.
reviews.raw_body:
Not a fan of what that tiering code is causing :/

But I suppose this will do; Mel?

2026-09-17.patch_summary: This patch prevents VMA PID activity from gating promotion in the NUMA scheduling algorithm. It does this by allowing periodic scans of inactive VMAs, even if they have not been recently accessed. This change is necessary to prevent starvation of placement scans and ensure that memory is properly tiered. The patch also introduces a new field to track the sequence ID of socket-placement scans. With this change, a large shmem VMA was no longer skipped during scanning, resulting in more efficient memory usage on a system with 768 GB of DRAM and 256 GB of CXL memory running two database workloads.

reviews.author: David (Arm)
reviews.summary: Reviewer David expressed strong dissatisfaction with the complexity of the promo_only() computation and requested a simpler solution.
reviews.raw_body:
This is all rather ... messy. I mean, just look at that promo_only() computation ...

There must be a cleaner way ;)
-- 
Cheers,

David

reviews.author: Gregory Price (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledges that the patch is not perfect and needs improvement, specifically to make the scan sequence logic less confusing in numab=3 mode.
reviews.raw_body:
I tried 3 or 4 different ways, this is the least ugly thing I could come
up with :\

The scan sequence thing is particularly confusing, and numab=3 mode
(NORMAL|TIERING) makes trying to reason about this whole thing really
painful.

I can see about making it at least a bit easier on the eyes.

~Gregory
